text: By definition, a sequence (a_n) of real numbers is a Cauchy sequence if:
choices: it is bounded and its terms eventually increase
for every eps>0 there exists N such that |a_n - a_m| < eps whenever n,m >= N
for every eps>0 there exists N such that |a_{n+1} - a_n| < eps whenever n >= N
it converges to a rational limit
explanation: Cauchy means all sufficiently late terms lie within eps of one another, i.e. |a_n - a_m| < eps for all large n,m. Requiring only consecutive terms to get close is strictly weaker: the harmonic partial sums satisfy it yet diverge. Boundedness/monotonicity and convergence to a rational are neither necessary nor the definition.
